observed_mechanics: 0x004b09bf / 0x004b09c1: CMP ECX,[EAX] then JZ 0x004b09f9 - assigning the value already held skips the entire body and falls through to the return, so self-assignment is a complete no-op

0x004b09c6 / 0x004b09c8: the outgoing pointer is copied into [EBP-4] before anything else happens; this is the re-entrancy temporary, because the store at 0x004b09e4 will overwrite the field the release has to read
0x004b09cb / 0x004b09cf: the incoming pointer is null-tested, so a null assignment is legal and costs nothing
0x004b09d4 / 0x004b09d9: two-step load of the incoming pointer's vtable slot +0x04; 0x004b09d6 reloads the pointer into ECX so the call is a thiscall with the pointee as receiver
0x004b09dc: CALL EAX with no stack arguments and no push at all, so slot +0x04 takes none
0x004b09e4: the store happens strictly between the acquire and the release, which is the ordering that makes the sequence safe when the incoming and outgoing objects are related
0x004b09ea / 0x004b09f1 / 0x004b09f4: the saved temporary, not the field, is the receiver of slot +0x08, so the release acts on the pre-store value
0x004b09f7: CALL EAX, again with no arguments
0x004b09ff: C2 04 00 is RET 4, so the callee pops the argument
0x00573c9f in FUN_00573c00 is the inlined mirror image: MOV dword ptr [EBX],0 / MOV EAX,[ECX] / MOV EDX,[EAX+8] / CALL EDX, which proves slot +0x08 is the release side

0x00573cce: PUSH EDI / MOV ECX,EBX / CALL 0x004b09b0 with EBX = the cEditor word at +0xCCh, i.e. the holder is used in place as a one-word field
0x005738df / 0x005738e0: PUSH EAX / LEA ECX,[ESI+0xd0] / CALL 0x004b09b0, so the same function assigns the holder at +0xD0h from the return value of a slot +0x28 call

semantic_contract: The receiver is a single-word intrusive reference holder. Given a replacement pointer, the function does nothing at all if the replacement is the pointer already held, and returns the holder. Otherwise it saves the outgoing pointer, acquires the replacement through the replacement's vtable slot +0x04 when the replacement is non-null, writes the replacement into the holder, then releases the saved outgoing pointer through its vtable slot +0x08 when it is non-null, and returns the holder. The acquire strictly precedes the store and the release strictly follows it, and the release acts on the saved value rather than on the field, so a callee that writes back through the holder during either indirect call cannot lose the outgoing reference. The function never dereferences a null pointer, never writes anywhere except the holder's one word, and never reads a global.
classification_rationale: The complete 32-instruction body, the frame, the RET 4 stack discipline, the single field offset, the self-assignment guard, both null tests, the acquire/store/release ordering and the return value are all read directly from the disassembly, and the two slot roles are corroborated from two independent inlined copies of the same pattern elsewhere in the binary. STRONG rather than BOUNDED because nothing material about the behaviour is left open: the receiver layout is one word, the callees are indirect and are correctly left as opaque ports, and the pointee's class is not needed to state the contract. The EASTL intrusive_ptr identification is recorded as an SDK correspondence and is deliberately not part of the claim.
semantic_findings: The body is a structural match for EASTL 3.02.01's intrusive_ptr<T>::operator=(T*), including the explicit re-entrancy temporary that EASTL's own source comments on.

The direction of each virtual slot is established from the binary, not assumed: +0x04 is called on the value being stored and +0x08 on the value being dropped, and 0x00573c9f shows the +0x08 call on a value that was just removed from a holder.
The function returns the holder, not the assigned pointer, which lets every callsite ignore the result.

The holder is used in place, as a bare one-word field of a larger object: cEditor+0xCCh and cEditor+0xD0h are the two disassembled sites, and both are the offsets the SDK gives mpActivePart and mpMovingPart.

The address has no vtable references, so this is one out-of-line template instantiation rather than a shared folded body - the opposite situation to the reference-count release at 0x007b86e0, and the reason the two targets classify differently.
unresolved_questions: Which pointee type is the template argument? EditorRigblock is the best-supported candidate from the two cEditor field offsets, but the 9 undisassembled callsites were not checked and could name a different instantiation.

Are the slot +0x04 and +0x08 callees really AddRef and Release, or two differently-named methods that happen to be called in these directions? Only the direction is proved by the binary; the names come from the SDK's DefaultRefCounted declaration.

Why does the erase loop at 0x004b06a0 walk the array assigning each cell its own value? Every iteration takes the early exit, so the loop is a no-op in the observed build. Its source-level intent is not recoverable from the code.
Is the argument always a raw pointer, or is there a second overload taking a pointer-to-pointer that was folded into this one? No such overload was found among the 11 code references.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this function. The acquire/store/release order is proved statically but its purpose - which re-entrant write-back it defends against - has not been observed.
The +0x04 and +0x08 callees have never been resolved on a concrete receiver, so the reference-count names remain inferred.

validation.byte_exactness: Not byte-identical and not claimed to be. The reconstruction is an extern "C" two-parameter port, so the receiver arrives on the stack rather than in ECX and the epilogue is a bare RET instead of RET 4; clang also allocates three callee-saved registers where the original uses none. The instruction sequence - compare, save, null-test, indirect call, store, null-test, indirect call, return - is the same in the same order with the same field offset and the same branch polarity.
